name: Latino Student Union
description: Latino student union is a group where students from Latino or Hispanic origins can come together to celebrate Latino/hispanic culture, learn and share experiences, and build a sense a community for all in attendance. LSU will be a welcoming place for students interested in learning and growing their connection to their culture. We will learn about Latino tradition, history, food, music, and the impact of Latinos on society and vise versa. The club will be open to all students and will provide a safe, welcoming, and comfortable environment where every student can feel seen and respected. The full purpose of LSU is to allow students to feel more connected, represented, and supported. For many students whose families come from Latin American countries, the group can be a place where they feel closer to their culture and heritage, while navigating a new environment.
targetAudience: Students interested in Latino/Hispanic culture.
detailedDescription: Latino Student Union is a group where students from Latino or Hispanic origins can come together to celebrate Latino/Hispanic culture, learn and share experiences, and build a sense of community for all in attendance. The club explores Latino tradition, history, food, music, and the impact of Latinos on society and vice versa, while welcoming all students and providing a safe, welcoming, and comfortable environment where every student can feel seen and respected. Its purpose is to allow students to feel more connected, represented, and supported, and for many students whose families come from Latin American countries, it can be a place where they feel closer to their culture and heritage while navigating a new environment.

name: Wayzata Computer Science Group
description: We get together weekly and teach member computer science topics. We focus on Python primarily during the beginning of the year and do fun projects that help them apply their learning. We foster teamwork with goals of incorporating group projects and team hackathons. Later in the year we are planning to introduce many other computer science aspects and fields like machine learning, cybersecurity, web developments, and agentic uses of artificial intelligence. The goal of these introductory lessons later in the year is to spark curiosity and set members up so that they can dive deeper into these topics themselves if they believe it is a topic of interest or a future career. We are hoping to get a guest speaker or two to let members get a real word understanding of how computer science is still being applied, but that part hasn't been figured out yet. We've been a club for many years but this year are hoping to do more then ever before for our members.
targetAudience: Students interested in coding and computer science careers.
detailedDescription: Wayzata Computer Science Group meets weekly to teach members computer science topics, focusing on Python early in the year with fun projects that apply what members learn. It fosters teamwork through group projects and team hackathons, and later in the year introduces other computer science fields such as machine learning, cybersecurity, web development, and agentic uses of artificial intelligence, so members can dive deeper into whichever topics interest them as a possible career.

name: Wayzata Inventors Group
description: Wayzata Inventors Group offers students the chance to design, build, and test innovative engineering projects in a collaborative, hands-on environment. Members tackle challenges ranging from structural design projects such as bridges and towers to more advanced experimental systems, developing strong problem-solving, creativity, and technical thinking skills. A central focus is guiding students through the development of official science-fair projects, supporting team formation based on shared interests, idea generation, research, prototyping, and testing, with structured mentorship to prepare for regional, state, and international competitions, including the International Science and Engineering Fair. The group aims to create a space where students pursue ambitious ideas, gain real project experience, and work toward producing high-quality, competition-ready research.
targetAudience: Students interested in engineering projects and science fair competitions.

name: Wayzata K-Pop Group

We dive into Korean culture, practice the language, play interactive team games, and learn choreography covers. By keeping things highly organized throughout the 2026–2027 school year, we plan to show the WHS Activities Office that our group has the consistency and student passion to deserve official school sponsorship!
targetAudience: Students interested in K-pop and Korean culture.
